body: Fixed in 3025e0326c: both rotation descriptions (the install.sh header and the README auth section) now state that a rotation updates both token copies and then restarts pm-dispatch.service — the unit reads the env file only at start, so without a restart the new token is rejected and the old one stays valid.

Fixed in 3025e0326c: OpenCodeError now carries the upstream httpStatus recorded by api(), and getSession returns null only when httpStatus === 404 — the decision no longer reads message text. Regression test in test/opencode.test.ts: a 500 whose body contains '(HTTP 404)' still rejects as OpenCodeError.

Fixed in 3025e0326c: QueueClient.getTask throws QueueError on a non-OK response (the read route answers 502); null is reserved for a successful empty result, so a PostgREST 401/5xx no longer reports an existing task as not found. Covered by new tests in test/queue.test.ts.

Fixed in 3025e0326c: handleGetTask catches the allowlist AuthError from assertCallerRepo and returns the identical 404 body as a missing task — an ID probe can no longer distinguish a denied task from a missing one or learn its repo. Authorization behavior on every other route is unchanged.

Fixed in 3025e0326c: handleGetSession wraps decodeURIComponent and throws ValidationError on malformed percent-encoding, so the route answers 400 instead of 500. Covered by a new test in test/server.test.ts (GET /v1/sessions/%ZZ → 400).

Fixed in 3025e0326c: handleGetSession is caller-aware now. For a dispatch-launched session it resolves the launching task via the new QueueClient.findTaskBySessionId (the task's progress.session_id) and applies the task route's allowlist gate to that task's repo — removing a repo from DISPATCH_REPO_ALLOWLIST closes its sessions too — and a denied session answers the same 404 as a missing one (no title, directory, or repo name). The lookup fails closed: a PostgREST failure throws QueueError (route answers 502) rather than skipping the gate. Sessions with no dispatch task carry no repo association in any record, so the gate covers exactly the dispatch-launched surface this route exists for (#5555).

Fixed in 3025e0326c: OpenCodeClient.api wraps fetch rejections as OpenCodeError, so a refused connection reaches handleGetSession's OpenCodeError branch and answers the documented 502 instead of falling through to the generic 500. Regression test in test/opencode.test.ts: getSession against a closed loopback port rejects with OpenCodeError.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve session repo authorization after task bindings clear**

When a dispatch-launched session's task expires or parks, the queue removes `progress.session_id` without deleting the OpenCode session (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/migration-0023.sql:56–61,195–202`). Because `findTaskBySessionId()` searches only that live binding, subsequent reads find no task and skip repo authorization. If the session's repo is removed from the allowlist, a still-authenticated caller can therefore continue retrieving its title and directory with HTTP 200, contrary to the revocation behavior documented above. Preserve a durable session-to-repo association rather than treating a missing live binding as an unscoped session.

Fixed in fafcc12754. findTaskBySessionId now checks two bindings, live first: progress.session_id, then the durable progress.session_cleared.session_id record that migration-0023 leaves on the task row when it clears a binding on park/lease-expiry. A session whose task has unbound therefore still resolves to its launching task, and the repo gate in handleGetSession applies exactly as for a live binding (denied answers as 404); a failed cleared-binding lookup still fails closed with QueueError (route answers 502). New tests in test/queue.test.ts cover the cleared-binding fallback (including the exact PostgREST field queried) and the fail-closed path. Full dispatch suite: bun test 190 pass; bunx tsc --noEmit clean (this commit also fixes the pre-existing fetch-stub cast errors that were failing tsc on this branch).
